licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: HMOs with five or more people in two or more households need a mandatory licence. Smaller HMOs with three or four sharers need no licence but must follow the HMO management and fire safety rules.

housing: South Staffordshire is a rural and commuter district wrapped around the west and north of Wolverhampton and the Black Country, mostly Green Belt. Homes are mainly inter-war and post-war semis, bungalows and detached houses in large villages such as Codsall, Perton, Wombourne and Penkridge, with Georgian cottages in Brewood and Kinver. Private renting is among the lowest in England, at about one household in ten. There are no towns of any size, so few shared houses.
checkinTips: Post-war semis and bungalows in Codsall, Perton and Wombourne: photograph gardens, fences, garages and driveways, which tenants are often expected to keep up.
Former mining villages such as Cheslyn Hay and Great Wyrley: record any cracks in walls or ceilings and doors that stick, which may come from old ground movement.
Period cottages in Brewood and Kinver: photograph damp on solid walls, beams, chimney breasts and any wood burner.
Canal-side homes along the Shropshire Union and Staffordshire and Worcestershire canals: check for damp, condensation and mould in ground-floor rooms.
Rural homes off the gas grid: record the oil tank and gauge level or LPG tank, and any septic tank or treatment plant cover.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact South Staffordshire Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect homes and take action against landlords.
